comment: The states on the map of 1 September 1939. ic is industry in 'factories': a blend of GDP 1938 (Harrison 1998; Maddison), Bairoch's share of world manufacturing 1938 and Kennedy's relative war potential 1937, as the historiker's pre-check lists them (docs/pruefer/historiker_vorpruefung_1939.md, table 3) -- GDP alone overstates the farming states (the Soviet Union, Poland, Rumania). pop is millions in the borders of 1939. quality is how well the army fought for its numbers, by year: training, officers, doctrine, equipment; our own judgement from the campaigns (filled in), not a measured figure. navy and air are one number each for now (rules.json, sea). colour is the map's, from the tradition of printed war maps; no emblem of any party or ideology is drawn anywhere in this game (the anwalt's pre-check, docs/pruefer/anwalt_vorpruefung.md). capitulation is the share of victory points lost at which a state gives up once its capital is gone. aggression is how readily its generals attack, by year: 1 attacks at the odds rules.json names, less wants better odds -- France and Britain sat behind the Maginot Line until May 1940 (the Saar offensive of September 1939 went eight kilometres), the Red Army of 1941 could not attack, that of 1943 did nothing else (filled in). divisionCost scales what a division costs to raise: the Red Army of 1941-42 raised some four hundred new divisions, thin in equipment, from its trained reserves. mobilisation is the share of the men of military age the army gets: Britain manned a great navy, air force and war industry first.

countries.name: Germany
countries.comment: With Austria (1938), the Sudetenland (1938), the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia (1939) and Memel (1939): 79.4 million by the census of May 1939 plus 7.4 in the Protectorate. GDP 351 (Altreich) + 24 + about 21. Field grey.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.comment: GDP 284; the Dominions and India are not on this map and are counted in its industry and its fuel from overseas. The red of the British Empire on printed maps.

countries.name: France
countries.comment: GDP 186; Kennedy 4.2, Bairoch 4.4. Its divisions fought well where they stood; its command could not move them in time (hence 0.8). Gave up in June 1940 with most of its land still its own: hence the low share.

countries.name: Soviet Union
countries.comment: GDP 359, Kennedy 14.0, Bairoch 9.0. The officer corps was gutted by the purges of 1937-38 and the army showed it in Finland in 1939 and in 1941; by 1943 it had learned. A plain red.

countries.name: Italy
countries.comment: GDP 141, Kennedy 2.5, Bairoch 2.8. Of 67 divisions on 1 September 1939 ten were complete (Knox).

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.comment: A client state under the treaty of protection of 23 March 1939; its field army attacked Poland beside the German 14th Army.

countries.name: Rumania
countries.comment: At its widest: with Bessarabia, all Bukovina, all Transylvania and southern Dobruja.

countries.name: Spain
countries.comment: Exhausted by the civil war that ended in April 1939: GDP about 45 against 62 in 1935.

countries.name: Luxemburg
countries.comment: Unarmed and neutral; its steel (1.44 Mt in 1938) is its weight.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.comment: Gave up on the day it was invaded, 9 April 1940.

countries.name: Finland
countries.comment: Held nine Soviet divisions on the Isthmus with six in the winter of 1939-40.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.comment: Kaunas is the provisional capital: Wilno is Polish, Memel German since March 1939.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.comment: A sovereign kingdom; by the treaty of 1936 British troops stand on the Canal and in war the country's ports and roads are Britain's to use. It broke with Germany on 3 September 1939 and declared war only in 1945: here it stands with the Allies and its own small army does not march.

countries.name: Iran
countries.comment: The press of 1939 still wrote Persia.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.comment: Riyadh lies south of the map's edge; the Nejd's northern town stands in for it. Its two brigades of tribal levies are filled in, not attested.

countries.name: Afghanistan
countries.comment: Only its western corner is on the map.

countries.name: Vichy France
countries.comment: Does not exist on 1 September 1939: made by the armistice of June 1940 (scenario, outcomes).
